title: How to better structure the artifacts of a java library with plugins
body_excerpt: Let's say I have a library, which provides two independent plugin interfaces, 2 implementations per plugin, and one parent POM file. There are also some abstract tests in the "core", which the plugins have to implement and pass to be considered compliant. From code perspective, the plugin interfaces don't depend on core at all. Only core depends on plugins. My assumptions are: the core abstractions go into the "core" artifact and its tests are packaged in a test-jar. each implementation of a "plugin" goes into a separate artifact (4 artifacts in this example). the parent POM also goes into a separate artifact. I have considered several options about how to structure the dependencies between each artifact, which can be boiled down to these 2: Leave it at just 6 artifacts. Every "plugin" depends on "core". Every "plugin" and "core" all depend on parent artifact. This makes it possible for the library users to only specify 2 artifacts in their pom.xml/build.gradle, because "core" is a transitive dependency. BUT, given I have some changes to the "core" which cause a version bump, I would have to update every plugin implementaton to bump the dependency version. Also, if users didn't specify the core explicitly, they now depend on outdated core. Extract plugin interfaces into separate artifacts, so that implementations no longer depend on core.
